_comment: Which session the operator is sent to first, when several need them (#261, #667).
The terminal has had this since #261, behind `n`. The dashboard grew it with
#667, and the ordering is the one rule the two must state identically: a queue
served in two different orders is worse than one window not having a queue.
Two rules, in this order. A raised call jumps ahead of every inferred attention
state, because the session said so itself where waiting/error/stalled are
deductions (ADR-0010, #389); among calls, the oldest `call_at` wins. Otherwise
the oldest `status_changed_at` among the attention states wins — how long the
session has been blocked, not how recently it was seen, since the watcher
refreshes `last_seen_at` every tick and would flatten the queue.
`attention` is the daemon's answer (ADR-0011), never re-derived by a client.
file and must agree case for case. `want` is the id, or "" for nothing to jump to.

cases.name: the one that has been blocked longest, not the one seen longest ago
a raised call jumps ahead of an older inferred state
among calls, the oldest call wins
a session both calling and blocked is still a call
